Accepted proof:
Source: Simon 6.1 (Λ^n with the inner product making e^{i_1}∧⋯∧e^{i_n} orthonormal, 6.1.15) and 6.3.4–3.5 (|v_1∧⋯∧v_n| = J); these are the algebraic facts behind "M_W(τ(M,θ,ξ)) = ∫_{M∩W}θ dH^n" (6.3.2(3)) and the Jacobian bound in step 5 of the parent proof.
1. Notation. 𝓘 := the strictly increasing maps I : Fin n → Fin P; e_k := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ k; for I ∈ 𝓘, α_I := α(e_{I 1}, …, e_{I n}); by definition |α|_E = (Σ_{I∈𝓘} α_I²)^{1/2} (the sum over all I with the StrictMono filter). For v = (v_1, …, v_n) let V be the P×n matrix V_{k,j} := ⟨e_k, v_j⟩ = v_j(k), and for I ∈ 𝓘 let V_I be the n×n matrix (V_I)_{a,j} := v_j(I a).
2. Expansion. α(v) = Σ_{I∈𝓘} α_I·det V_I. Proof: write v_j = Σ_k v_j(k)e_k and expand by multilinearity: α(v) = Σ_{f : Fin n → Fin P} (Π_j v_j(f j))·α(e_{f 1}, …, e_{f n}). Terms with f not injective vanish (α alternating, repeated argument). Each injective f is uniquely f = I∘σ with I ∈ 𝓘 (the increasing enumeration of its range) and σ a permutation, and α(e_{I∘σ}) = sgn(σ)α_I. So α(v) = Σ_I α_I Σ_σ sgn(σ) Π_j v_j(I(σ j)) = Σ_I α_I det V_I by the Leibniz formula.
3. Cauchy–Binet. Σ_{I∈𝓘} (det V_I)² = det(VᵀV) = det(⟨v_i, v_j⟩)_{i,j}. Proof: det(VᵀV) = Σ_σ sgn(σ) Π_i (Σ_k V_{k,i}V_{k,σ i}) = Σ_{f : Fin n → Fin P} (Π_i V_{f i, i})·Σ_σ sgn(σ) Π_i V_{f i, σ i} = Σ_f (Π_i V_{f i, i})·det(V_f), where V_f is the n×n matrix (V_{f a, j})_{a,j}. det V_f = 0 unless f is injective, and for f = I∘σ, det V_f = sgn(σ) det V_I (row permutation). Hence det(VᵀV) = Σ_I det V_I·Σ_σ sgn(σ) Π_i V_{I(σ i), i} = Σ_I (det V_I)² (Leibniz formula again).
4. Part (1). By step 2 and the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality in ℝ^𝓘, |α(v)| ≤ (Σ_I α_I²)^{1/2}(Σ_I (det V_I)²)^{1/2} = |α|_E·(det(⟨v_i, v_j⟩))^{1/2} by step 3 (the Gram determinant is ≥ 0, being a sum of squares).
5. Part (2). For n = 0 take α the constant 0-covector with value 1: |α|_E = 1 (𝓘 consists of the empty map) and α() = 1. For n ≥ 1 let α(u_1, …, u_n) := det(⟨τ_a, u_b⟩)_{a,b}; it is multilinear, alternating and continuous, hence an n-covector, and α(τ) = det(⟨τ_a, τ_b⟩) = det I = 1. Moreover α_I = det(⟨τ_a, e_{I b}⟩)_{a,b} = det(T_I) with T the P×n matrix of τ (transposes have equal determinants), so by step 3 applied to v = τ: |α|_E² = Σ_I det(T_I)² = det(⟨τ_a, τ_b⟩) = 1. Hence |α|_E = 1 ≤ 1.
6. Degenerate cases are covered: if n > P then 𝓘 = ∅, |α|_E = 0, every n-covector vanishes (n vectors in ℝ^P are dependent) and there is no orthonormal n-family.
proof_key_steps: Expansion α(v) = Σ_I α(e_I) det V_I by multilinearity and alternation.
Cauchy–Binet: Σ_I (det V_I)² = det(v_i·v_j).
Cauchy–Schwarz gives (1); the covector u ↦ det(⟨τ_a, u_b⟩) gives (2).

Accepted proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, Remark 3.2(1) (chapter-06.txt lines 755–756, stated without proof). Tools: the Upper Density Theorem, Ch. 1, 3.6 with Remark 3.7(2) (chapter-01.txt lines 700–722; SimonGMT Chapter01/DensityComparison.lean), and the fact that approximate tangent spaces only depend on a set up to sets of zero density, Ch. 3, 1.4–1.5 and Remark 1.8(1) (chapter-03.txt lines 77–108, 298–310). Throughout Hⁿ = μHE[n], η_{x,r}(y) := r⁻¹(y − x) (SimonGMT blowUpMap), and Hⁿ(η_{x,r}(E)) = r^{−n}Hⁿ(E) for all E (μHE[n] is translation invariant and n-homogeneous: Mathlib euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀). Let R₁ = (M₁, θ₁, ξ₁) and R₂ = (M₂, θ₂, ξ₂) be IMReps in U representing S and T.
1. Local finiteness. For compact K ⊆ U, Hⁿ(M_i ∩ K) ≤ ∫_{M_i∩K} θ_i dHⁿ < ∞ since θ_i ≥ 1 on M_i. Hence every Borel A ⊆ M₁ ∪ M₂ has Hⁿ(A ∩ K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U.
2. (F1) If A ⊆ M₁ ∪ M₂ is Borel, then ρ^{−n}Hⁿ(A ∩ B_ρ(y)) → 0 as ρ ↓ 0 for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ U ∖ A. Proof: let V_j be open sets with compact closures in U and ⋃_j V_j = U; apply Ch. 1, 3.6 to the finite Borel-regular measure Hⁿ⌞(A ∩ V_j) to get the conclusion for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ V_j ∖ A (for y ∈ V_j and small ρ, B_ρ(y) ⊆ V_j), and take the union of the countably many exceptional null sets.
3. (F2) Let A, A' be Hⁿ-measurable, y ∈ U, s > 0 with Hⁿ(A ∩ B_s(y)), Hⁿ(A' ∩ B_s(y)) < ∞, ρ^{−n}Hⁿ((A Δ A') ∩ B_ρ(y)) → 0, and HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A y Q. Then HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A' y Q. Proof: finrank Q = n is unchanged. For f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) with spt f ⊆ B_L(0) and 0 < r < s/L both blow-up integrals are finite and |∫_{η_{y,r}(A')} f dHⁿ − ∫_{η_{y,r}(A)} f dHⁿ| ≤ sup|f|·Hⁿ(η_{y,r}(A Δ A') ∩ B_L(0)) = sup|f|·r^{−n}Hⁿ((A Δ A') ∩ B_{Lr}(y)) → 0, so the blow-up integrals of A' converge to ∫_Q f dHⁿ as well.
4. (F3) If ζ and ζ' are both unit orientations of the same n-dimensional subspace Q (IsUnitOrientationOf), then ζ' = ±ζ: if ζ(α) = σα(τ) and ζ'(α) = σ'α(τ') with τ, τ' orthonormal bases of Q, then τ' = τB for an orthogonal n×n matrix B, and multilinearity plus the alternating property give α(τ') = det(B)α(τ) with det B = ±1.
5. Normalization. Changing ξ_i on an Hⁿ⌞M_i-null set changes neither the integrals in R_i.Represents nor the almost-everywhere statement `orients`; so we may assume ξ₁, ξ₂ Borel measurable. Put E := M₁ ∩ M₂. For increasing I : {1,…,n} → {1,…,P} let e^I ∈ Λⁿ(ℝ^P) be the covector e^I(v₁,…,vₙ) = det(⟨e_{I(a)}, v_b⟩)_{a,b}; these form a basis of Λⁿ(ℝ^P), so an n-vector ζ (a linear functional on Λⁿ) is determined by the numbers ζ(e^I). If ζ(α) = ±α(τ) for an orthonormal frame τ, then ζ ≠ 0 (the covector (v₁,…,vₙ) ↦ det(⟨τ_a, v_b⟩) takes the value ±1 under ζ), hence Σ_I ζ(e^I)² > 0.
6. Common tangent planes. For Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ M_i the approximate tangent space T_yM_i exists and ξ_i(y) orients it. By F1 (with A = M₁ ∖ M₂ and A = M₂ ∖ M₁) and F2 (with A = M_i, A' = E, since M_i Δ E ⊆ M₁ ∖ M₂ or ⊆ M₂ ∖ M₁ and y ∉ these sets), for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ E the space T_yE exists and T_yM₁ = T_yE = T_yM₂. By F3, for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ E, ξ₂(y) = σ'ξ₁(y) for some σ' ∈ {±1}; then Σ_I ξ₁(y)(e^I)ξ₂(y)(e^I) = σ'Σ_I ξ₁(y)(e^I)² with Σ_I ξ₁(y)(e^I)² > 0 (step 5), so σ' = σ(y) := sign(Σ_I ξ₁(y)(e^I)·ξ₂(y)(e^I)), a Borel function, and ξ₂(y) = σ(y)ξ₁(y). The set of points of E where any of these properties fails is Hⁿ-null, hence contained in a Borel null set; let G ⊆ E be the Borel complement of that null set in E.
7. New data. On G put d := θ₁ − σθ₂ ∈ ℤ and G' := {y ∈ G : d(y) ≠ 0}. Define the Borel set M := (M₁ ∖ M₂) ∪ (M₂ ∖ M₁) ∪ G', the measurable m : ℝ^P → ℕ with m = θ₁ on M₁ ∖ M₂, m = θ₂ on M₂ ∖ M₁, m = |d| on G', m = 0 elsewhere, and the Borel ζ with ζ = ξ₁ on M₁ ∖ M₂, ζ = −ξ₂ on M₂ ∖ M₁, ζ = sign(d)ξ₁ on G', ζ = 0 elsewhere.
8. IMRep fields. M ⊆ M₁ ∪ M₂ ⊆ U; M is countably n-rectifiable (subset of the union of two countably n-rectifiable sets: SimonGMT CountablyRectifiable.mono, countablyRectifiable_iUnion); m ≥ 1 on M; m ≤ θ₁1_{M₁} + θ₂1_{M₂} (on G', |d| ≤ θ₁ + θ₂), so ∫_{M∩K} m dHⁿ ≤ ∫_{M₁∩K} θ₁ + ∫_{M₂∩K} θ₂ < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U; ζ is Borel, hence a.e. strongly measurable. Orientation property for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ M: (i) y ∈ M₁ ∖ M₂: M Δ M₁ ⊆ M₂ and, by F1 with A = M₂, M₂ has density 0 at a.e. y ∉ M₂, so F2 gives T_yM = T_yM₁, oriented by ξ₁(y) = ζ(y); (ii) y ∈ M₂ ∖ M₁: symmetrically T_yM = T_yM₂, oriented by ξ₂(y) and hence by ζ(y) = −ξ₂(y) (IsUnitOrientationOf allows either sign); (iii) y ∈ G': M Δ M₁ = (M₂ ∖ M₁) ∪ (E ∖ G') is a Borel set not containing y, so by F1 it has density 0 at a.e. such y, and F2 gives T_yM = T_yM₁, oriented by ξ₁(y) and hence by ζ(y) = ±ξ₁(y).
9. Representation. For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) (all integrands are integrable, being bounded by (θ₁1_{M₁} + θ₂1_{M₂})·sup|ω|·1_{tsupport ω}): (S − T)(ω) = ∫_{M₁}θ₁ξ₁(ω) − ∫_{M₂}θ₂ξ₂(ω) = ∫_{M₁∖M₂}θ₁ξ₁(ω) + ∫_{M₂∖M₁}θ₂(−ξ₂)(ω) + ∫_E (θ₁ξ₁ − θ₂ξ₂)(ω) dHⁿ. On G, θ₁ξ₁ − θ₂ξ₂ = (θ₁ − σθ₂)ξ₁ = |d|·sign(d)ξ₁, which vanishes on G ∖ G', and E ∖ G is Hⁿ-null; so the last integral equals ∫_{G'} |d| sign(d)ξ₁(ω) dHⁿ. Hence (S − T)(ω) = ∫_M m ζ(ω) dHⁿ, i.e. (M, m, ζ) is an IMRep in U representing S − T, and S − T is integer multiplicity.

Approximate tangent spaces are unchanged by modifications of density zero, so on M₁ ∩ M₂ the tangent planes agree a.e. and ξ₂ = ±ξ₁.

Accepted proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, Remark 3.2(3) (chapter-06.txt lines 763–765: M_W(T) = ∫_{M∩W} θ dHⁿ for open W) and Ch. 6, 2.11–2.12 (chapter-06.txt lines 295–307: spt T = spt μ_T). The book states both without proof; a complete proof follows. Notation: M = R.carrier, θ = R.mult, ξ = R.orient, μ_R = R.measure = θHⁿ⌞M. For an n-covector α, |α| = (Σ_I α(e_I)²)^{1/2} is the Euclidean coefficient norm (covectorEuclideanNorm; I runs over strictly increasing multi-indices, e_I = (e_{i_1}, …, e_{i_n})), and dx^I denotes the coordinate covector with dx^I(e_J) = δ_{IJ}. ⟨α, ξ(x)⟩ means ξ(x)(α).
1. Pointwise algebra. Let x ∈ M be a point where R.orients holds: there are an orthonormal family τ₁, …, τₙ and s ∈ {1, −1} with ⟨α, ξ(x)⟩ = s·α(τ₁, …, τₙ) for every α. Expanding τ_j = Σ_i τ_j^i e_i, multilinearity and alternation give α(τ₁, …, τₙ) = Σ_I α(e_I)·det(τ^I), where det(τ^I) is the n×n minor of the matrix (τ_j^i) on the rows I; by the Cauchy–Binet formula Σ_I det(τ^I)² = det(τᵀτ) = 1. By Cauchy–Schwarz, |⟨α, ξ(x)⟩| ≤ |α| for every α. The covector ξ^♭(x) := Σ_I ⟨dx^I, ξ(x)⟩ dx^I has coefficients s·det(τ^I), hence |ξ^♭(x)| = 1 and ⟨ξ^♭(x), ξ(x)⟩ = Σ_I det(τ^I)² = 1. (For n = 0 the only I is empty: |α| = |α()|, ξ(x) = ±evaluation, ξ^♭(x) = ±1.) Since R.orients holds Hⁿ-a.e. on M and μ_R ≪ Hⁿ⌞M, these facts hold μ_R-a.e. The field x ↦ ξ^♭(x) is μ_R-a.e. strongly measurable, being a continuous linear function of the a.e. strongly measurable ξ (R.aestronglyMeasurable_orient).
2. Integral formula. For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) the function x ↦ θ(x)⟨ω(x), ξ(x)⟩ is Hⁿ⌞M-integrable: it is a.e. strongly measurable, vanishes off the compact set spt ω ⊆ U, is bounded by θ·sup|ω| a.e. (step 1), and ∫_{M∩spt ω} θ dHⁿ < ∞ (R.locallyIntegrable_mult). Hence T(ω) = R.action(ω) = ∫ ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dμ_R (integral with respect to the density θ).
3. Upper bound. Let W be open and ω admissible for M_W(T) (ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), spt ω ⊆ W, |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x). By step 1, ⟨ω(x), ξ(x)⟩ ≤ |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for μ_R-a.e. x, and ω = 0 off W, so T(ω) ≤ μ_R(W) by step 2. Taking the supremum, M_W(T) ≤ μ_R(W).
4. Lower bound. Let W be open and t a real number with t < μ_R(W); we construct an admissible ω with T(ω) > t, which proves M_W(T) ≥ μ_R(W) (also when μ_R(W) = ∞). Put G := W ∩ U (open). Since M ⊆ U, μ_R(G) = μ_R(W). μ_R is a Borel measure, finite on compact subsets of U; restricted to the open σ-compact set G it is a Radon measure (Simon Ch. 1, 1.15), hence inner regular by compact sets and outer regular on sets of finite measure. Fix η > 0 and a compact K ⊆ G with μ_R(K) > t + 4η. (a) Lusin (Simon Ch. 1, 1.17): there is a compact K' ⊆ K with μ_R(K ∖ K') < η such that ξ^♭ restricted to K' is continuous, and |ξ^♭| = 1, ⟨ξ^♭, ξ⟩ = 1 μ_R-a.e. on K'. (b) There is an open V with K' ⊆ V, V̄ compact, V̄ ⊆ G, and μ_R(V ∖ K') < η. (c) Extend the coefficients of ξ^♭ on K' continuously to ℝ^P (Tietze), compose with the radial retraction of Λⁿ(ℝ^P) onto its closed unit ball for |·|, and multiply by a continuous χ with 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1, χ = 1 on K', spt χ ⊆ V. The resulting continuous g has compact support in V, |g| ≤ 1 everywhere and g = ξ^♭ on K'. (d) Let g_ε := φ_ε ∗ g (coefficientwise convolution with a standard mollifier). For 0 < ε < dist(spt g, ℝ^P ∖ V), g_ε is C^∞ with compact support in V ⊆ W ∩ U, |g_ε(x)| ≤ ∫ φ_ε(x − y)|g(y)| dy ≤ 1 by convexity of the norm, and g_ε → g uniformly as ε → 0; so g_ε is admissible for M_W(T). (e) By steps 2 and 1, T(g_ε) = ∫⟨g_ε, ξ⟩ dμ_R ≥ ∫_{K'}⟨g, ξ⟩ dμ_R − ∫_{V∖K'}|⟨g, ξ⟩| dμ_R − sup|g_ε − g|·μ_R(V̄) ≥ μ_R(K') − η − sup|g_ε − g|·μ_R(V̄) ≥ μ_R(K) − 2η − sup|g_ε − g|·μ_R(V̄) > t + 2η − sup|g_ε − g|·μ_R(V̄). As μ_R(V̄) < ∞, T(g_ε) > t for small ε. Together with step 3 this proves (i): M_W(T) = μ_R(W).
5. Support. By definition (SimonGMT GeometricCurrentOn.support; Simon 2.11) spt T = U ∖ Z, where Z is the union of all open W with W̄ compact, W̄ ⊆ U and T(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with spt ω ⊆ W. Recall x ∈ spt μ_R iff μ_R(B) > 0 for every neighbourhood B of x. (a) If x ∈ U ∩ spt μ_R and x ∈ Z, choose W in the union with x ∈ W; every admissible form for M_W(T) has T(ω) = 0, so M_W(T) = 0, hence μ_R(W) = 0 by (i), contradicting x ∈ spt μ_R. So U ∩ spt μ_R ⊆ spt T. (b) spt T ⊆ U by definition. If x ∈ U ∖ spt μ_R, choose r > 0 with μ_R(B_r(x)) = 0 and B̄_r(x) ⊆ U (U open). For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with spt ω ⊆ B_r(x), T(ω) = ∫⟨ω, ξ⟩ dμ_R = 0 by step 2; so B_r(x) is one of the sets forming Z, x ∈ Z and x ∉ spt T. Hence spt T = U ∩ spt μ_R, which is (ii).
proof_key_steps: For a unit simple n-vector ξ, |⟨α, ξ⟩| ≤ |α| (Cauchy–Binet), with equality for the dual covector ξ^♭.
T(ω) = ∫⟨ω, ξ⟩ dμ_R, so admissible forms give T(ω) ≤ μ_R(W).
Lusin, Tietze extension, retraction and mollification of ξ^♭ give admissible forms with T(ω) arbitrarily close to μ_R(W).
The mass formula identifies the zero region of T with the complement of spt μ_R in U.

2. Borel sign on the overlap. Define σ(x) := 1 if ξ̃₂(x) = ξ̃₁(x) and σ(x) := −1 otherwise. The set {ξ̃₂ = ξ̃₁} is Borel (both maps are strongly measurable into the metrizable space Λ_n(ℝ^P)), so σ : ℝ^P → ℤ is Borel. Claim: for μ-a.e. x, x ∈ M₁ ∩ M₂ ⇒ ξ̃₂(x) = σ(x)ξ̃₁(x). In the first case σ(x) = 1; in the second case, if ξ̃₂(x) ≠ ξ̃₁(x) then σ(x) = −1 and ξ̃₂(x) = −ξ̃₁(x), while if ξ̃₂(x) = ξ̃₁(x) we are in the first case. In all cases ξ̃₂(x) = σ(x)ξ̃₁(x). (This equality test replaces the parent proof's coordinate test Σ_I⟨e^I, ξ₁⟩⟨e^I, ξ₂⟩ ≥ 0, whose verification needs the Cauchy–Binet identity; only the property ξ̃₂ = σξ̃₁ a.e. on M₁ ∩ M₂ is used below.)

   c(x) := p₁θ₁(x)1_{M₁}(x) + p₂θ₂(x)(σ(x)1_{M₁∩M₂}(x) + 1_{M₂∖M₁}(x)),   ζ(x) := ξ̃₁(x) if x ∈ M₁, ζ(x) := ξ̃₂(x) otherwise.
c is Borel (ℤ is countable with the discrete σ-algebra; c is built from the Borel maps θ₁, θ₂, σ and the indicators of the Borel sets M₁, M₂), ζ is strongly measurable (piecewise on the Borel set M₁), c = 0 off A, and since at most one of 1_{M₁∩M₂}(x), 1_{M₂∖M₁}(x) is nonzero and |σ| = 1,
   (3a) |c(x)| ≤ |p₁|θ₁(x)1_{M₁}(x) + |p₂|θ₂(x)1_{M₂}(x) for all x.

4. Pointwise identity. Let x satisfy [x ∈ M₁ ∩ M₂ ⇒ ξ̃₂(x) = σ(x)ξ̃₁(x)]. Then p₁1_{M₁}(x)θ₁(x)ξ̃₁(x) + p₂1_{M₂}(x)θ₂(x)ξ̃₂(x) = c(x)ζ(x). Cases: if x ∉ A both sides are 0; if x ∈ M₁ ∖ M₂ both sides equal p₁θ₁(x)ξ̃₁(x); if x ∈ M₂ ∖ M₁ both sides equal p₂θ₂(x)ξ̃₂(x); if x ∈ M₁ ∩ M₂ the left side is p₁θ₁(x)ξ̃₁(x) + p₂θ₂(x)σ(x)ξ̃₁(x) = (p₁θ₁(x) + p₂θ₂(x)σ(x))ξ̃₁(x) = c(x)ζ(x).

5. Definition of R. Let M' := {x ∈ A : c(x) ≠ 0}, θ'(x) := |c(x)| ∈ ℕ and ξ'(x) := sgn(c(x))·ζ(x). Since |c|·sgn(c) = c, and c(x) = 0 whenever x ∉ M' (either x ∉ A, or x ∈ A with c(x) = 0), we have
   (5a) 1_{M'}(x)θ'(x)ξ'(x) = c(x)ζ(x) for every x ∈ ℝ^P.

6. R = (M', θ', ξ') is an IMRep in U:
   (a) M' is Borel (A and c are Borel) and M' ⊆ A ⊆ U.
   (b) M₁ ∪ M₂ is countably n-rectifiable (SimonGMT countablyRectifiable_iUnion applied to the sequence M₁, M₂, M₂, …), hence so is M' ⊆ M₁ ∪ M₂ (CountablyRectifiable.mono).
   (c) θ' = |c| is Borel and θ' ≥ 1 on M'.
   (d) For compact K ⊆ U, by (3a): ∫⁻_{M'∩K} θ' dμ ≤ |p₁|∫⁻_{M₁∩K} θ₁ dμ + |p₂|∫⁻_{M₂∩K} θ₂ dμ < ∞.
   (e) ξ' is strongly measurable (product of the Borel real function sgn∘c and ζ), hence AEStronglyMeasurable for μ⌞M'.
   (f) Orientation. M' is Borel, M' ⊆ U, and μ(M' ∩ K) ≤ μ(M₁ ∩ K) + μ(M₂ ∩ K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U. Apply the sibling lemma imrep_tangent_transfer with R := R₁, B := M' ∩ M₁, C := M': for μ-a.e. x ∈ M' ∩ M₁ there is Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M' x Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ₁ x) Q; for a.e. such x also ξ̃₁(x) = ξ₁(x) (step 1), so ξ'(x) = sgn(c(x))ξ₁(x) with sgn(c(x)) = ±1 (c(x) ≠ 0 on M'). A unit orientation multiplied by −1 is a unit orientation of the same plane (same τ, the other sign alternative), so IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ' x) Q. Likewise apply imrep_tangent_transfer with R := R₂, B := M' ∖ M₁ (⊆ M₂ because M' ⊆ M₁ ∪ M₂), C := M': for μ-a.e. x ∈ M' ∖ M₁ there is Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M' x Q, IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ₂ x) Q and ξ'(x) = sgn(c(x))ξ̃₂(x) = ±ξ₂(x). Since M' = (M' ∩ M₁) ∪ (M' ∖ M₁), the orients property holds μ⌞M'-a.e.

7. The identity. By steps 1 and 2, for μ-a.e. x: (i) x ∈ M_i ⇒ ξ̃_i(x) = ξ_i(x) for i = 1, 2, and (ii) x ∈ M₁ ∩ M₂ ⇒ ξ̃₂(x) = σ(x)ξ̃₁(x). At every such x, (5a), step 4 and (i) give
   1_{M'}(x)θ'(x)ξ'(x) = c(x)ζ(x) = p₁1_{M₁}(x)θ₁(x)ξ̃₁(x) + p₂1_{M₂}(x)θ₂(x)ξ̃₂(x) = p₁1_{M₁}(x)θ₁(x)ξ₁(x) + p₂1_{M₂}(x)θ₂(x)ξ₂(x)
(the indicator 1_{M_i}(x) vanishes when x ∉ M_i). This is the asserted identity, μ-a.e. ∎
proof_key_steps: Replace ξ₁, ξ₂ by Borel versions ξ̃₁, ξ̃₂ equal to them a.e. on M₁, M₂.
Borel sign σ := 1 on {ξ̃₂ = ξ̃₁}, −1 elsewhere; by overlap_orientation_sign, ξ̃₂ = σξ̃₁ a.e. on M₁ ∩ M₂.
c := p₁θ₁1_{M₁} + p₂θ₂(σ1_{M₁∩M₂} + 1_{M₂∖M₁}), ζ := ξ̃₁ on M₁, ξ̃₂ off M₁; then p₁1_{M₁}θ₁ξ̃₁ + p₂1_{M₂}θ₂ξ̃₂ = cζ.
M' := {c ≠ 0} ∩ (M₁ ∪ M₂), θ' := |c|, ξ' := sgn(c)ζ satisfy every IMRep field; orientation via imrep_tangent_transfer on M' ∩ M₁ and M' ∖ M₁.
1_{M'}θ'ξ' = cζ everywhere, hence equals p₁1_{M₁}θ₁ξ₁ + p₂1_{M₂}θ₂ξ₂ a.e.

subproblems.title: An integer multiplicity triple defines a current
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P, and R = (M, θ, ξ) an IMRep of U (Simon 6.3.1 data). Then there is T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) such that T(ω) = R.action ω = ∫_M θ(x)⟨ω(x), ξ(x)⟩ dHⁿ(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) (R.Represents T). Here T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) means a GeometricCurrentOn U n: a linear functional on 𝒟ⁿ(U) with T(ω_j) → 0 whenever ω_j → 0 in Simon's test-form topology (TestFormOnConverges).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n), ∃ T : GeometricCurrentOn U n, R.Represents T
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse note (context, not part of the numbered proof): this child is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.dtc_imrep_current of DAG node root.density_and_tangent_cones-a1.localize-a1.imrep_current-a1 (status accepted, candidate commit 642d7450f79f28435ddba02f9c815e2208bcee00). Its frozen type is byte-identical to the lean_statement above, so the controller reuses that node and creates no new node. Use in the selected node: sibling current_pushforward (its step 3) turns the pushed-forward triple R' into the current Y = q_#(S − T) (parent step 2).

Accepted proof:
Source: Simon 6.3.1 (chapter-06.txt lines 733–753), where formula (‡) is asserted to define a current. The parent proof uses this in step 6.6 for X̃ = τ(M_X ∩ K, θ_X, ξ_X) in U.
Notation: μ := Hⁿ⌞M = μHE[n].restrict M; for a covector α, ‖α‖ is its operator norm as a continuous alternating map.
1. Unit orientations have norm at most one. By the field orients, for μ-a.e. x there are a subspace Q and an orthonormal family τ = (τ₁, …, τₙ) such that ξ(x)(α) = α(τ) for all α, or ξ(x)(α) = −α(τ) for all α (IsUnitOrientationOf). Then for every covector α, |ξ(x)(α)| = |α(τ₁, …, τₙ)| ≤ ‖α‖·∏ᵢ|τᵢ| = ‖α‖ (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm; the product is empty when n = 0).
2. Measurability. For every continuous n-form ω, the function x ↦ θ(x)ξ(x)(ω(x)) is μ-a.e. strongly measurable. Indeed θ is measurable (ℕ-valued), ξ is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (field aestronglyMeasurable_orient), ω is continuous, and evaluation (L, α) ↦ L(α) is continuous because it is bounded bilinear (isBoundedBilinearMap_apply; Continuous.comp_aestronglyMeasurable₂).
3. θ is integrable over compact sets. Let K be compact with K ⊆ U. Then 1_K θ is μ-integrable: it is measurable, and ∫ 1_K θ dμ = ∫_{M∩K} θ dHⁿ < ∞ by the field locallyIntegrable_mult, since (Hⁿ⌞M)⌞K = Hⁿ⌞(K ∩ M) (Measure.restrict_restrict; integrable_indicator_iff). Write C_K := ∫ 1_K θ dμ ∈ [0, ∞).
4. Integrability of the integrand. Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), K := tsupport ω (compact, ⊆ U), and B := sup_y ‖ω(y)‖ < ∞ (ω is continuous with compact support). By step 1, for μ-a.e. x, |θ(x)ξ(x)(ω(x))| ≤ θ(x)‖ω(x)‖ ≤ B·1_K(x)θ(x); if x ∉ K then ω(x) = 0. By steps 2–3 and domination (Integrable.mono'), x ↦ θ(x)ξ(x)(ω(x)) is μ-integrable.
5. Linearity. Define T(ω) := R.action ω for ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). Each ξ(x) is linear, so the integrand for ω + η is the sum of the integrands for ω and η. Both are integrable by step 4, so T(ω + η) = T(ω) + T(η) (integral_add). The integrand for cω is c times the integrand for ω, so T(cω) = cT(ω) (integral_const_mul). Thus T is a linear functional on 𝒟ⁿ(U), and R.Represents T holds by definition.
6. Sequential continuity. Let ω_j → 0 in 𝒟ⁿ(U) (TestFormOnConverges ω_j 0). Then there is a compact K ⊆ U with tsupport ω_j ⊆ K for all j, and every derivative converges uniformly on K. For the 0-th derivative (‖D⁰g(x)‖ = ‖g(x)‖ and D⁰0 = 0) this says ε_j := sup_{x∈K} ‖ω_j(x)‖ → 0. By step 1, for μ-a.e. x, |θ(x)ξ(x)(ω_j(x))| ≤ ε_j·1_K(x)θ(x), since ω_j(x) = 0 off K. Hence |T(ω_j)| ≤ ε_j·C_K (norm_integral_le_of_norm_le with step 3). Given ε > 0, choose N such that ‖ω_j(x)‖ < ε/(C_K + 1) for all j ≥ N and x ∈ K. Then |T(ω_j)| ≤ εC_K/(C_K + 1) < ε for j ≥ N, so T(ω_j) → 0.
7. By steps 5 and 6, T is a GeometricCurrentOn U n with T(ω) = R.action ω for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). ∎
proof_key_steps: Unit orientations satisfy |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ ‖α‖ for a.e. x in M.
For a test form ω the integrand is a.e. strongly measurable and dominated by sup|ω|·1_{spt ω}·θ, which is integrable by local integrability of θ. Hence ω ↦ ∫_M θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ is linear.
If ω_j → 0 in 𝒟ⁿ(U) with supports in a compact K, then |T(ω_j)| ≤ sup_K|ω_j|·∫_{M∩K} θ → 0, so T is a current.

subproblems.title: Orthogonal projection does not increase the pairing with a unit orientation (Hadamard bound)
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, let V, Q ⊆ ℝ^P (Euclid P) be linear subspaces, let q := V.starProjection be the orthogonal projection of ℝ^P onto V, let ξ ∈ Λ_m(ℝ^P) (MultiVector P m, a continuous linear functional on m-covectors) be a unit orientation of Q (IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q: there is an orthonormal family τ = (τ_1, …, τ_m) spanning Q such that ξ(β) = β(τ_1, …, τ_m) for every m-covector β, or ξ(β) = −β(τ_1, …, τ_m) for every m-covector β), and let α be an m-covector on ℝ^P. Write α∘q for the m-covector (v_1, …, v_m) ↦ α(qv_1, …, qv_m) (α.compContinuousLinearMap q). Then |ξ(α∘q)| ≤ |α|_E, where |α|_E = covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_{i_1<⋯<i_m} α(e_{i_1}, …, e_{i_m})²)^{1/2} is the Euclidean coefficient norm.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (V Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (ξ : MultiVector P m) (α : Covector (Euclid P) m), IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q → |ξ (α.compContinuousLinearMap V.starProjection)| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 of the parent proof ("|Λ_m q ξ_S(x)| = |qτ_1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ qτ_m| ≤ Π|qτ_i| ≤ 1 for a unit simple ξ_S(x) = ±τ_1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ τ_m (Hadamard's inequality, |q| ≤ 1)"). This is Simon 7.3.1, footnote 2 (chapter-07.txt lines 358–362: orthogonal projection onto the subspace does not increase area) in the algebraic form of Simon 6.3.4–3.5 (chapter-06.txt lines 789–806: |d f_# ξ| = J^M f).
Sibling used: gram_bounds (covectorEuclideanNorm_gram_bounds, part (1)): |α(v_1, …, v_m)| ≤ |α|_E·√det(⟨v_i, v_j⟩)_{i,j} for all v_1, …, v_m ∈ ℝ^P.
1. (Unpack the orientation.) By IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q choose an orthonormal family τ = (τ_1, …, τ_m) in ℝ^P and ε ∈ {1, −1} with ξ(β) = ε·β(τ_1, …, τ_m) for every m-covector β. Take β := α∘q. Then ξ(α∘q) = ε·α(qτ_1, …, qτ_m), because (α.compContinuousLinearMap q)(τ) = α(fun i => q(τ_i)). Put v_i := qτ_i, so |ξ(α∘q)| = |α(v_1, …, v_m)|.
2. (Gram bound.) By gram_bounds (1), |α(v_1, …, v_m)| ≤ |α|_E·√(det G), where G := (⟨v_i, v_j⟩)_{i,j=1}^m is the Gram matrix of v.
3. (0 ≤ G ≤ I.) G is a real symmetric m×m matrix. For every c ∈ ℝ^m, linearity of q gives cᵀGc = ‖Σ_i c_i v_i‖² = ‖q(Σ_i c_iτ_i)‖². An orthogonal projection is a contraction: ‖w‖² = ‖qw‖² + ‖w − qw‖², i.e. Mathlib Submodule.norm_starProjection_apply_le. Since τ is orthonormal, 0 ≤ cᵀGc ≤ ‖Σ_i c_iτ_i‖² = Σ_i c_i² = cᵀc.
4. (det G ≤ 1.) By the spectral theorem for real symmetric matrices (Mathlib Matrix.IsHermitian.eigenvalues_eq, Matrix.IsHermitian.det_eq_prod_eigenvalues), G has an orthonormal eigenbasis u_1, …, u_m of ℝ^m with real eigenvalues λ_k = u_kᵀGu_k, and det G = Π_k λ_k. Step 3 with c = u_k gives 0 ≤ λ_k ≤ u_kᵀu_k = 1. Hence 0 ≤ det G ≤ 1. For m = 0, G is the empty matrix and det G = 1.
5. (Conclusion.) By step 4, √(det G) ≤ 1. Since |α|_E ≥ 0 (covectorEuclideanNorm_nonneg), steps 1–2 give |ξ(α∘q)| = |α(v)| ≤ |α|_E·√(det G) ≤ |α|_E. (If m > P there is no orthonormal family τ of length m, and the hypothesis is never satisfied.) ∎
proof_key_steps: Unpack the unit orientation: |ξ(α∘q)| = |α(qτ_1, …, qτ_m)| for an orthonormal family τ.
Sibling gram_bounds: |α(qτ)| ≤ |α|_E·√det G, where G is the Gram matrix of qτ_1, …, qτ_m.
q is a contraction and τ is orthonormal, so 0 ≤ cᵀGc ≤ cᵀc. Hence the eigenvalues of G lie in [0, 1] and det G ≤ 1.
Therefore |ξ(α∘q)| ≤ |α|_E.

subproblems.title: A triple whose weight lives on a subspace V is invariant under pull-back by the orthogonal projection onto V
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, let V ⊆ ℝ^P (Euclid P) be a linear subspace with orthogonal projection q (V.starProjection), and let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an integer multiplicity triple in ℝ^P (IMRep univ m) whose weight μ_R = θ·H^m⌞M (R.measure) satisfies μ_R(ℝ^P ∖ V) = 0. Then R.action(q^#ω) = R.action(ω) for every m-form ω on ℝ^P (every map ω : ℝ^P → Λ^m(ℝ^P), DifferentialForm (Euclid P) m). Here q^#ω(x)(v_1, …, v_m) := ω(qx)(qv_1, …, qv_m) (affinePullbackForm q 0 ω), R.action(η) := ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(η(x)) dH^m(x) and H^m = μHE[m].
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (R : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) m) (V : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), R.measure ((V : Set (Euclid P))ᶜ) = 0 → ∀ ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) m, R.action (affinePullbackForm V.starProjection 0 ω) = R.action ω
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 of the parent proof ("μ_T(ℝ^P ∖ V) = 0 and H^m(M ∖ V) = 0; consequently H^m-a.e. x ∈ M has its approximate tangent plane T_x contained in V, so Λ_m q ξ(x) = ξ(x) for μ_T-a.e. x"). This is the identity q_#T = T behind Simon 7.3.1, footnote 2 (chapter-07.txt lines 358–362).
Approximate tangent spaces follow Simon Ch. 3, Definition 1.4 (chapter-03.txt lines 77–86), in SimonGMT's form. HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt m M x Q means: dim Q = m, and for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P), ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f dH^m → ∫_Q f dH^m as r ↓ 0, where η_{x,r}(y) = r^{-1}(y − x) (blowUpMap).
1. (H^m(M ∖ V) = 0.) The set ℝ^P ∖ V is open, because the finite-dimensional subspace V is closed. Hence μ_R(ℝ^P ∖ V) = ∫⁻_{ℝ^P∖V} θ d(H^m⌞M) = ∫⁻_{M∖V} θ dH^m (withDensity_apply, Measure.restrict_restrict). θ is ℕ-valued and θ > 0 on M (mult_pos), so θ ≥ 1 on M. Therefore H^m(M ∖ V) ≤ ∫⁻_{M∖V} θ dH^m = μ_R(ℝ^P ∖ V) = 0.
2. (Good set.) Let G be the set of x ∈ M ∩ V for which some subspace Q satisfies both HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt m M x Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ(x)) Q. R.orients holds for H^m⌞M-a.e. x, and step 1 gives H^m(M ∖ V) = 0. So H^m⌞M-almost every x lies in G.
3. (Tangent planes lie in V.) Let x ∈ G with its subspace Q; we show Q ⊆ V. If m = 0 then dim Q = 0, so Q = {0} ⊆ V. Let m ≥ 1 and suppose some v ∈ Q ∖ V. Since V is closed, δ := dist(v, V) > 0. Define f(y) := max(0, δ/2 − ‖y − v‖). Then f is continuous, f ≥ 0, f(v) = δ/2, and f vanishes outside the compact ball B̄(v, δ/2), so f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P). Also f(y) = 0 for y ∈ V, because ‖y − v‖ ≥ δ there.
 (a) For every r > 0, ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f dH^m = 0. Let y = η_{x,r}(z) with z ∈ M and y ∉ V. Then z ∉ V, since x ∈ V gives η_{x,r}(z) = r^{-1}(z − x) ∈ V whenever z ∈ V. Hence {y ∈ η_{x,r}(M) : f(y) ≠ 0} ⊆ η_{x,r}(M) ∖ V ⊆ η_{x,r}(M ∖ V). The map η_{x,r} is Lipschitz with constant r^{-1} and H^m(M ∖ V) = 0, so H^m(η_{x,r}(M ∖ V)) = 0. (Lipschitz images of H^m-null sets are H^m-null: Mathlib LipschitzWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le, and μHE[m] is a positive multiple of μH[m].) The set {f ≠ 0} is open, hence measurable. So its measure for H^m restricted to η_{x,r}(M) is H^m({f ≠ 0} ∩ η_{x,r}(M)) = 0, f = 0 almost everywhere for that restricted measure, and the integral is 0.
 (b) Apply HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt m M x Q to f: ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f dH^m → ∫_Q f dH^m as r ↓ 0. By (a), ∫_Q f dH^m = 0.
 (c) dim Q = m. Choose an orthonormal basis of Q and the corresponding linear isometry ι : ℝ^m → ℝ^P (Euclid m → Euclid P) with range Q. μHE is preserved by isometries (Mathlib Isometry.map_euclideanHausdorffMeasure / Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image), and μHE[m] on ℝ^m is Lebesgue measure L^m. Hence ∫_Q f dH^m = ∫_{ℝ^m} f(ιz) dL^m(z). Put z₀ := ι^{-1}(v). If ‖z − z₀‖ < δ/4 then ‖ιz − v‖ < δ/4, so f(ιz) > δ/4. Therefore ∫_Q f dH^m ≥ (δ/4)·L^m(B(z₀, δ/4)) > 0, which contradicts (b). So Q ⊆ V.
4. (Pointwise identity on G.) Let x ∈ G with Q as above. By IsUnitOrientationOf choose an orthonormal family τ = (τ_1, …, τ_m) spanning Q and ε ∈ {±1} with ξ(x)(β) = ε·β(τ) for all m-covectors β. Since x ∈ V and every τ_i ∈ Q ⊆ V, we have qx = x and qτ_i = τ_i (Mathlib Submodule.starProjection_eq_self_iff). So q^#ω(x) = ω(0 + qx)∘Λ^m q = ω(x)∘Λ^m q, and ξ(x)(q^#ω(x)) = ε·ω(x)(qτ_1, …, qτ_m) = ε·ω(x)(τ_1, …, τ_m) = ξ(x)(ω(x)).
5. (Conclusion.) By steps 2 and 4, θ(x)·ξ(x)(q^#ω(x)) = θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(x)) for H^m⌞M-a.e. x. Functions that agree almost everywhere have the same Bochner integral, with no integrability needed (Mathlib integral_congr_ae for μHE[m].restrict M). Therefore R.action(q^#ω) = ∫_M θ ξ(q^#ω) dH^m = ∫_M θ ξ(ω) dH^m = R.action(ω). ∎
proof_key_steps: μ_R(ℝ^P ∖ V) = 0 and θ ≥ 1 on M give H^m(M ∖ V) = 0.
At H^m-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ V an approximate tangent plane Q exists and ξ(x) is a unit orientation of Q.
Q ⊆ V: a C_c bump vanishing on V has zero blow-up integrals over η_{x,r}(M), but it would have positive integral over Q if Q ⊄ V.
q is the identity on V ⊇ Q, so ξ(x)(q^#ω(x)) = ξ(x)(ω(x)) a.e. on M; integrate.

subproblems.title: Representations of currents that agree on an open set have the same weight there
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ and S, T ∈ 𝒟_m(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ m), with integer multiplicity representations R_S, R_T (IMRep univ m; R_S.Represents S, R_T.Represents T). Let O ⊆ ℝ^P be open such that S(ω) = T(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P) with tsupport ω ⊆ O. Then the weights agree on O: μ_{R_S}⌞O = μ_{R_T}⌞O, i.e. R_S.measure.restrict O = R_T.measure.restrict O.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (S T : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) m) (RS RT : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) m) (O : Set (Euclid P)), IsOpen O → RS.Represents S → RT.Represents T → (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) m, tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) m) ⊆ O → S ω = T ω) → RS.measure.restrict O = RT.measure.restrict O
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 5 of the parent proof ("S = T on the open set ℝ^P ∖ K', so μ_S = μ_T there"), which the supplied proof derives from im_mass_measure (c) on ℝ^P ∖ K'. Here it is derived instead from Simon Ch. 6, 3.2(3) (chapter-06.txt lines 763–765: M_W(τ(M, θ, ξ)) = ∫_{M∩W} θ dH^m for open W), in the form of sibling mass_support (dor_imrep_massOn_eq_measure_and_support), plus uniqueness of measures.
1. By mass_support with U = ℝ^P (open), S.massOn G = μ_{R_S}(G) and T.massOn G = μ_{R_T}(G) for every open G ⊆ ℝ^P.
2. For every open G ⊆ O, S.massOn G = T.massOn G. By definition (Simon 6.2.5, SimonGMT massOn), massOn G is the supremum of ofReal(S(ω)) over the set 𝒜(G) (massAdmissibleOn univ m G) of test forms ω with tsupport ω ⊆ G and |ω(x)|_E ≤ 1 for all x. The set 𝒜(G) is the same for S and T. For ω ∈ 𝒜(G), tsupport ω ⊆ G ⊆ O, so S(ω) = T(ω) by hypothesis. The two sets of values coincide, and so do their suprema.
3. Put ν_S := μ_{R_S}⌞O and ν_T := μ_{R_T}⌞O. For every open G, Measure.restrict_apply (G is measurable) and steps 1–2 applied to the open set G ∩ O ⊆ O give ν_S(G) = μ_{R_S}(G ∩ O) = S.massOn(G ∩ O) = T.massOn(G ∩ O) = μ_{R_T}(G ∩ O) = ν_T(G).
4. (Local finiteness.) For every n ∈ ℕ, ν_S(B(0, n)) ≤ μ_{R_S}(B̄(0, n)) = ∫⁻_{M_S∩B̄(0,n)} θ_S dH^m < ∞. This uses the field locallyIntegrable_mult of R_S on the compact set B̄(0, n), with withDensity_apply and Measure.restrict_restrict. The same holds for ν_T.
5. The open subsets of ℝ^P form a π-system generating the Borel σ-algebra (borel_eq_generateFrom_isOpen, isPiSystem_isOpen). Moreover ℝ^P = ⋃_n B(0, n), with each B(0, n) open and of finite ν_S-measure. Two measures that agree on a generating π-system containing such a countable cover are equal (Mathlib Measure.ext_of_generateFrom_of_iUnion). By step 3, ν_S = ν_T. ∎
proof_key_steps: Mass equals weight on open sets (sibling mass_support).
The masses of S and T agree on open subsets of O, since the admissible forms and their values coincide.
So the restricted weights agree on all open sets. Both are finite on balls, hence they are equal by π-system uniqueness.

subproblems.title: Linear push-forward of an integer multiplicity triple carried by a compact set is integer multiplicity (Simon 6.3.3–3.9)
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ with m ≥ 1, let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an integer multiplicity triple in ℝ^P (IMRep univ m), let L : ℝ^P → ℝ^P be linear (Euclid P →L[ℝ] Euclid P), and let K ⊆ ℝ^P be compact with μ_R(ℝ^P ∖ K) = 0 (R.measure Kᶜ = 0). Then there is an integer multiplicity triple R' = (N, θ', ξ') in ℝ^P (IMRep univ m) with N ⊆ L(K) and R'.action(ω) = R.action(L^#ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P) (TestFormOn univ m). Here L^#ω(x)(v_1, …, v_m) := ω(Lx)(Lv_1, …, Lv_m) (affinePullbackForm L 0 ω), so R.action(L^#ω) = ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(Lx)∘Λ^m L) dH^m(x). In Simon's notation: L_#τ(M, θ, ξ) = τ(N, θ', ξ').
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (R : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) m) (L : Euclid P →L[ℝ] Euclid P) (K : Set (Euclid P)), 0 < m → IsCompact K → R.measure Kᶜ = 0 → ∃ R' : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) m, R'.carrier ⊆ L '' K ∧ ∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) m, R'.action (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) m) = R.action (affinePullbackForm L 0 (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) m))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, 3.3–3.9 (chapter-06.txt lines 770–860), Lemma 3.9: if f is locally Lipschitz and proper on spt T and T = τ(M, θ, ξ), then f_#T = τ(f(M), θ', ξ') is integer multiplicity. Here f = L is linear, so d^M L_x = L|T_xM, and the triple is carried by the compact set K, so L is proper on it. Steps B4–B10 below follow Simon 3.4–3.8: (3.4)–(3.5) are B4–B5, (3.6) is B9, and (3.7)–(3.8) are B6–B8 and B10.
Departure from the book. Simon's printed argument asserts without proof (3.7) that, for H^m-a.e. y, the approximate tangent space T_y(f(M)) exists and equals d^M f_x(T_xM) for every x ∈ f^{-1}(y) ∩ M_+. That gap is filled here by the parametrized-piece fact A7, proved from bilipschitz pieces and the Lipschitz area formula, which is the route of Federer 3.2.18–3.2.19. Simon's own route to such facts goes through the C^1-submanifold cover of Ch. 3, Lemma 1.2 and the proof of Theorem 1.6 (chapter-03.txt lines 25–143). That cover needs the C^1 Approximation Theorem of Ch. 2, 1.5 (chapter-02.txt line 165), which is not in the pinned library. The quantitative partition A5 supplies a positive lower Lipschitz constant on every piece. The proof cites no DAG declaration; every auxiliary fact is proved in Part A from the pinned libraries.
Library facts (pinned Mathlib 25730c7c and SimonGMT; the Lean proof adds the imports Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.AreaLipschitz and Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter01.DensityComparison, as accepted submissions already do):
(L1) Lipschitz area formula on injective pieces (SimonGMT Chapter02.weighted_area_formula_lipschitz_injOn). If F : ℝ^m → ℝ^P is Lipschitz, S ⊆ ℝ^m is Borel and F is injective on S, then ∫⁻_{F(S)} g dH^m = ∫⁻_S J_F(a)·g(F(a)) dL^m(a) for every g : ℝ^P → [0, ∞]. Applied to g⁺ and g⁻, this gives the same identity of Bochner integrals for every Borel real g with ∫_{F(S)} |g| dH^m < ∞.
(L2) Lipschitz image bound (SimonGMT Chapter02.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn). If φ is K-Lipschitz on a set S of a metric space, then H^m(φ(S)) ≤ K^m H^m(S). On ℝ^m, μHE[m] = L^m (Mathlib EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume). In particular, Lipschitz images of L^m-null sets are H^m-null.
(L3) Linear area formula and Jacobians:
- H^m(A(S)) = normDet(A)·L^m(S) for linear A : ℝ^m → ℝ^P and S ⊆ ℝ^m (Mathlib LinearMap.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_eq_normDet_mul_volume);
- J_F(a) := areaJacobianAt F a = normDet(DF(a));
- normDet(cA) = |c|^m normDet(A) (LinearMap.normDet_smul);
- normDet(A)² = det(⟨Ae_j, Ae_k⟩)_{j,k} (LinearMap.normDet_sq_eq_det_gram);
- normDet(A) = 0 iff A is not injective (LinearMap.normDet_eq_zero_iff_ker_ne_bot);
- J_F and areaRegularSet F = {a : F differentiable at a, DF(a) injective} are Borel (SimonGMT measurable_areaJacobianAt, measurableSet_areaRegularSet);
- H^m(F(ℝ^m ∖ areaRegularSet F)) = 0 for Lipschitz F (SimonGMT area_image_compl_regularSet_eq_zero).
(L4) Lusin–Souslin (Mathlib MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn): the image of a Borel subset of ℝ^m under a map that is continuous and injective on it is Borel.
(L5) Lebesgue differentiation (Mathlib IsUnifLocDoublingMeasure.ae_tendsto_average_norm_sub, applied to L^m): for h ∈ L¹_loc(ℝ^m), L^m-a.e. b satisfies ⨍_{B̄_ρ(b)} |h − h(b)| dL^m → 0 as ρ ↓ 0.
(L6) Upper density theorem (Simon Ch. 1, 3.6 and Remark 3.7(1), chapter-01.txt lines 700–710; SimonGMT Chapter01.simon_remark_3_7_hausdorff). If D ⊆ ℝ^P is Borel with H^m(D) < ∞, then H^m(D ∩ B̄_ρ(x))/ρ^m → 0 as ρ ↓ 0 for H^m-a.e. x ∉ D. SimonGMT states this for the literal outer measure simonHausdorffOuterMeasureReal m, and the following lemmas transfer it to μHE[m]:
- simonHausdorffMeasureReal_toOuterMeasure: that outer measure is the outer measure of simonHausdorffMeasureReal m;
- simonHausdorffMeasureReal_nat_eq_smul_euclideanHausdorffMeasure, simonAreaNormalization_pos, simonAreaNormalization_ne_top: that measure is c_m·μHE[m] with c_m := simonAreaNormalization m ∈ (0, ∞);
- simonHausdorffOuterMeasureReal_isBorelRegular: Borel sets are measurable for it;
- realUnitBallVolume_pos, realUnitBallVolume_ne_top: the density quotient uses closed balls and the constant realUnitBallVolume m ∈ (0, ∞).
Hence null sets and the vanishing of the quotient are the same as for μHE[m].
(L7) Uniqueness of approximate tangent spaces (SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique; Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(1)).
(L8) Partition into approximately linear pieces (Mathlib exists_partition_approximatesLinearOn_of_hasFDerivWithinAt), and the antilipschitz bound for injective linear maps (LinearMap.exists_antilipschitzWith).
(L9) Alternating maps:
- if τ is a basis of a space Q and β is an alternating m-form on Q, then β(w) = det(τ.toMatrix w)·β(τ) (AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det, Module.Basis.det_apply);
- an alternating map vanishes on linearly dependent families (AlternatingMap.map_linearDependent);
- |β(v_1, …, v_m)| ≤ ‖β‖·Π_j‖v_j‖ (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm).
Notation:
- m ≥ 1 (hypothesis). ℝ^m = Euclid m carries Lebesgue measure L^m; H^m = μHE[m] on ℝ^P.
- For F : ℝ^m → ℝ^P, DF(a) := fderiv ℝ F a and J_F(a) := normDet(DF(a)) ≥ 0.
- For a linear A : ℝ^m → ℝ^P, [A] is the m-vector β ↦ β(Ae_1, …, Ae_m), where e is the standard basis of ℝ^m.
- For an m-vector ζ, L_#ζ is the m-vector β ↦ ζ(β∘Λ^mL), where β∘Λ^mL := β.compContinuousLinearMap L. By the definition of affinePullbackForm, (L^#ω)(x) = ω(Lx)∘Λ^mL, so ξ(x)(L^#ω(x)) = (L_#ξ(x))(ω(Lx)).
- ‖β‖ is the operator norm of an m-covector, and η_{x,r}(y) := r^{-1}(y − x) (blowUpMap).
- "T_xY = Q" abbreviates HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt m Y x Q, and "unit orientation of Q" abbreviates IsUnitOrientationOf.
Part A. Auxiliary facts.
A1 (Blow-up scaling.) For x ∈ ℝ^P and r > 0, η_{x,r} is a homeomorphism of ℝ^P with η_{x,r}^{-1}(B̄_R(0)) = B̄_{rR}(x), and H^m(η_{x,r}(S)) = r^{-m}H^m(S) for every S ⊆ ℝ^P. Proof: η_{x,r} is the homothety with centre x and ratio r^{-1}, which multiplies H^m by r^{-m} (Mathlib euclideanHausdorffMeasure_homothety_image), followed by the isometry y ↦ y − x (Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image).
A2 (Null modifications.) If H^m(A ∖ B) = H^m(B ∖ A) = 0, then for every x and Q, T_xA = Q ⟺ T_xB = Q. Proof: for r > 0, η_{x,r} is a bijection, so η_{x,r}(A) △ η_{x,r}(B) = η_{x,r}(A △ B), which is H^m-null by A1. Hence H^m⌞η_{x,r}(A) = H^m⌞η_{x,r}(B), and the integrals in Simon Ch. 3, Definition 1.4 coincide for every f and r. The dimension condition is the same on both sides.
A3 (Locality.) Let A' ⊆ Y ⊆ ℝ^P be Borel with H^m(Y) < ∞. Then for H^m-a.e. x ∈ A' and every Q, T_xY = Q ⟺ T_xA' = Q. Proof:
- D := Y ∖ A' is Borel with H^m(D) < ∞, and A' ∩ D = ∅. By L6, H^m(D ∩ B̄_ρ(x))/ρ^m → 0 for H^m-a.e. x ∈ A'.
- Fix such an x, f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) with |f| ≤ c_f and f = 0 off B̄_R(0) (WLOG R ≥ 1), and r > 0. Since η_{x,r} is injective, η_{x,r}(Y) is the disjoint union of the Borel sets η_{x,r}(A') and η_{x,r}(D).
- By A1, H^m(η_{x,r}(Y) ∩ B̄_R(0)) = r^{-m}H^m(Y ∩ B̄_{rR}(x)) < ∞, so f is integrable on all three sets. Hence |∫_{η_{x,r}(Y)} f dH^m − ∫_{η_{x,r}(A')} f dH^m| = |∫_{η_{x,r}(D)} f dH^m| ≤ c_f H^m(η_{x,r}(D) ∩ B̄_R(0)) = c_f R^m·H^m(D ∩ B̄_{rR}(x))/(rR)^m → 0 as r ↓ 0.
- So for every f the two blow-up integrals converge to ∫_Q f dH^m together or not at all. The dimension conditions agree, hence T_xY = Q ⟺ T_xA' = Q.
A4 (Bilipschitz comparison.) Let F : ℝ^m → ℝ^P, S ⊆ ℝ^m and c > 0 satisfy c|a − a'| ≤ |F(a) − F(a')| for a, a' ∈ S. Then L^m(S) ≤ c^{-m}H^m(F(S)) (outer measures). Proof: F is injective on S, and the inverse φ : F(S) → S, φ(F(a)) = a, is c^{-1}-Lipschitz on F(S). By L2, L^m(S) = H^m(φ(F(S))) ≤ c^{-m}H^m(F(S)).
A5 (Quantitative partition.) Let G : ℝ^m → ℝ^P and B ⊆ ℝ^m Borel, with G differentiable at every b ∈ B and DG(b) injective. Then there are pairwise disjoint Borel sets C_l (l ∈ ℕ) with ⋃_l C_l = B, and constants d_l > 0 with d_l|a − a'| ≤ |G(a) − G(a')| for all a, a' ∈ C_l. Proof:
- If B = ∅, take C_l = ∅ and d_l = 1.
- Otherwise choose r(A) > 0 for every linear A : ℝ^m → ℝ^P. If A is injective, L8 gives K_A > 0 with |v| ≤ K_A|Av| for all v; put κ_A := 1/K_A and r(A) := κ_A/2. Otherwise put r(A) := 1.
- L8 (with s = B and f' = DG; HasFDerivWithinAt holds because G is differentiable on B) gives pairwise disjoint Borel t_l and linear A_l such that: B ⊆ ⋃_l t_l; |G(a) − G(a') − A_l(a − a')| ≤ r(A_l)|a − a'| for a, a' ∈ B ∩ t_l (ApproximatesLinearOn); and A_l = DG(y_l) for some y_l ∈ B, so A_l is injective.
- Put C_l := B ∩ t_l and d_l := κ_{A_l}/2. For a, a' ∈ C_l, |G(a) − G(a')| ≥ |A_l(a − a')| − (κ_{A_l}/2)|a − a'| ≥ κ_{A_l}|a − a'| − (κ_{A_l}/2)|a − a'| = d_l|a − a'|.
A6 (Bilipschitz pieces of a rectifiable set.) Let M₁ ⊆ ℝ^P be Borel and countably m-rectifiable. Then there are Lipschitz F_i : ℝ^m → ℝ^P, Borel B_i ⊆ ℝ^m and c_i > 0 (i ∈ ℕ) such that:
- c_i|b − b'| ≤ |F_i(b) − F_i(b')| for b, b' ∈ B_i;
- F_i is differentiable with injective derivative at every b ∈ B_i;
- the sets F_i(B_i) are Borel, pairwise disjoint and contained in M₁;
- H^m(M₁ ∖ ⋃_i F_i(B_i)) = 0.
Proof:
- By Simon Ch. 3, Definition 1.1 (SimonGMT CountablyRectifiable), M₁ ⊆ Z₀ ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝ^m) with H^m(Z₀) = 0 and each F_j Lipschitz.
- Reg_j := areaRegularSet F_j is Borel and H^m(F_j(ℝ^m ∖ Reg_j)) = 0 (L3). S_j := Reg_j ∩ F_j^{-1}(M₁) is Borel. Apply A5 to F_j on S_j, getting pieces S_{j,l} and constants c_{j,l}.
- Enumerate the pairs (j, l) by i ∈ ℕ and write F'_i, B'_i, c_i. Each F'_i(B'_i) is Borel (L4: F'_i is continuous, and injective on B'_i) and contained in M₁.
- Disjointify recursively: B_i := B'_i ∖ F'^{-1}_i(⋃_{i'<i} F'_{i'}(B_{i'})), which is Borel. Then F'_i(B_i) = F'_i(B'_i) ∖ ⋃_{i'<i} F'_{i'}(B_{i'}), these images are pairwise disjoint, and ⋃_i F'_i(B_i) = ⋃_i F'_i(B'_i) = M₁ ∩ ⋃_j F_j(Reg_j).
- Hence M₁ ∖ ⋃_i F'_i(B_i) ⊆ Z₀ ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝ^m ∖ Reg_j), which is H^m-null. Subsets of B'_i keep the lower Lipschitz bound and the differentiability. Rename F'_i as F_i.
A7 (Tangent spaces along a bilipschitz piece; the fact (TF).) Let:
- F : ℝ^m → ℝ^P be Λ-Lipschitz;
- B ⊆ ℝ^m be Borel and c > 0, with c|a − a'| ≤ |F(a) − F(a')| for a, a' ∈ B;
- F be differentiable at every b ∈ B with DF(b) injective;
- Y ⊆ ℝ^P be Borel with F(B) ⊆ Y and H^m(Y) < ∞.
Then for L^m-a.e. b ∈ B, T_{F(b)}Y = range DF(b).
Proof.
(1) F(B) is Borel (L4). For every Borel E ⊆ B, H^m(F(E)) = ∫_E J_F dL^m by L1 with g = 1, and this is ≤ Λ^m L^m(E) by L2.
(2) Put h := 1_B·J_F. It is Borel and locally integrable: for bounded Borel D, ∫_D h dL^m = H^m(F(B ∩ D)) ≤ Λ^m L^m(D) < ∞ by (1). By L5, for L^m-a.e. b, ⨍_{B̄_ρ(b)} |h − h(b)| dL^m → 0 as ρ ↓ 0.
(3) (Blow-up convergence and identification with range DF(b).) Fix b ∈ B satisfying (2), and put x := F(b), A := DF(b), Q := range A.
- A is injective, so dim Q = m, and by L8 there is κ > 0 with |Av| ≥ κ|v|. Also h(b) = J_F(b) = normDet(A).
- Let f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) with |f| ≤ c_f and f = 0 off B̄_R(0), where WLOG R ≥ 1. Put R₁ := max(R/c, R/κ) > 0 and D := B̄_{R₁}(0) ⊆ ℝ^m.
 (a) For r > 0 let G_r := η_{x,r}∘F, i.e. G_r(a) = r^{-1}(F(a) − F(b)). G_r is Lipschitz and injective on B, and η_{x,r}(F(B)) = G_r(B). Moreover J_{G_r}(a) = r^{-m}J_F(a) for every a. Where F is differentiable, DG_r(a) = r^{-1}DF(a), and L3 gives normDet(r^{-1}DF(a)) = r^{-m}normDet(DF(a)). Where F is not differentiable, neither is G_r (since F = F(b) + rG_r), and both Jacobians are normDet(0) = 0 (m ≥ 1).
 (b) If a ∈ B and |G_r(a)| ≤ R, then c|a − b| ≤ |F(a) − F(b)| ≤ rR. So G_r(B) ∩ B̄_R(0) ⊆ G_r(B ∩ B̄_{rR/c}(b)), and since G_r is (Λ/r)-Lipschitz, L2 gives H^m(G_r(B) ∩ B̄_R(0)) ≤ (Λ/r)^m L^m(B̄_{rR/c}(b)) < ∞. Hence f is H^m-integrable on G_r(B), and L1 applied to f⁺ and f⁻ gives ∫_{G_r(B)} f dH^m = ∫_B r^{-m}J_F(a)f(G_r(a)) dL^m(a).
 (c) Substitute a = b + rz, using Mathlib Measure.integral_comp_smul and the translation invariance of L^m. This gives ∫_{η_{x,r}(F(B))} f dH^m = ∫_{ℝ^m} h(b + rz)f(g_r(z)) dL^m(z), where g_r(z) := r^{-1}(F(b + rz) − F(b)) = G_r(b + rz). If h(b + rz)f(g_r(z)) ≠ 0, then b + rz ∈ B and |g_r(z)| ≤ R, so c|z| ≤ |g_r(z)| ≤ R and z ∈ D. So the integral is over D.
 (d) By L3, H^m⌞Q is the image of normDet(A)·L^m under A: for Borel S ⊆ ℝ^P, H^m(Q ∩ S) = H^m(A(A^{-1}S)) = normDet(A)·L^m(A^{-1}S). Therefore ∫_Q f dH^m = ∫_{ℝ^m} h(b)f(Az) dL^m(z). Here f(Az) ≠ 0 forces κ|z| ≤ |Az| ≤ R, so this integral is over D as well.
 (e) Subtracting, |∫_{η_{x,r}(F(B))} f dH^m − ∫_Q f dH^m| ≤ c_f∫_D |h(b + rz) − h(b)| dL^m(z) + h(b)∫_D |f(g_r(z)) − f(Az)| dL^m(z).
  - The first integral equals r^{-m}∫_{B̄_{rR₁}(b)} |h − h(b)| dL^m = L^m(B̄_{R₁}(0))·⨍_{B̄_{rR₁}(b)} |h − h(b)| dL^m, which → 0 by (2).
  - For the second, let ε > 0. Since f is uniformly continuous, there is δ_f > 0 with |f(u) − f(u')| < ε whenever |u − u'| < δ_f. Differentiability of F at b gives ρ₀ > 0 with |F(b + w) − F(b) − Aw| ≤ (δ_f/(2R₁))|w| for |w| ≤ ρ₀. For 0 < r ≤ ρ₀/R₁ and z ∈ D, |g_r(z) − Az| = r^{-1}|F(b + rz) − F(b) − A(rz)| ≤ δ_f/2. Hence |f(g_r(z)) − f(Az)| < ε, and the second integral is ≤ εL^m(D).
  So ∫_{η_{x,r}(F(B))} f dH^m → ∫_Q f dH^m as r ↓ 0, for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P). Since dim Q = m, this says T_{F(b)}F(B) = range DF(b).
(4) (Transfer to Y.) By A3 with A' := F(B) ⊆ Y, there is an H^m-null set Z ⊆ F(B) such that T_xY = Q ⟺ T_xF(B) = Q for every x ∈ F(B) ∖ Z and every Q. By A4, L^m({b ∈ B : F(b) ∈ Z}) ≤ c^{-m}H^m(Z) = 0. Together with (3), T_{F(b)}Y = range DF(b) for L^m-a.e. b ∈ B. ∎(A7)
A8 (Linear algebra of simple m-vectors; Simon 6.3.4–3.5.)
(i) Let Q ⊆ ℝ^P be an m-dimensional subspace with orthonormal basis τ = (τ_1, …, τ_m), and A : ℝ^m → ℝ^P linear with range A ⊆ Q. Write Ae_j = Σ_l a_{jl}τ_l. Then [A](β) = det(a)·β(τ_1, …, τ_m) for every m-covector β, and normDet(A) = |det a|.
 Proof: the restriction of β to Q is an alternating m-form on Q. The coordinate matrix of (Ae_j)_j in the basis τ is aᵀ, so L9 gives β(Ae_1, …, Ae_m) = det(a)β(τ). By L3 and the orthonormality of τ, normDet(A)² = det(⟨Ae_j, Ae_k⟩) = det(aaᵀ) = (det a)².
(ii) If A : ℝ^m → ℝ^P is injective and ζ is a unit orientation of Q := range A, then normDet(A) > 0 and [A] = ±normDet(A)·ζ.
 Proof: by IsUnitOrientationOf, ζ = ±[τ] for an orthonormal family τ spanning Q. Since dim Q = m, τ is an orthonormal basis of Q. By (i), [A] = det(a)[τ] with |det a| = normDet(A), which is > 0 by L3.
(iii) If A is injective, η_A := [A]/normDet(A) is a unit orientation of range A. Indeed, by (i) applied with any orthonormal basis τ of range A, [A] = ±normDet(A)[τ], so η_A = ±[τ].
(iv) Two unit orientations ζ = ±[τ] and ζ' = ±[τ'] of the same m-dimensional Q satisfy ζ' = ±ζ. Apply (i) to the map e_j ↦ τ'_j: [τ'] = det(o)[τ], where o is the change-of-basis matrix. By (i) and L3, (det o)² = normDet(e_j ↦ τ'_j)² = det(⟨τ'_j, τ'_k⟩) = 1, so det o = ±1. Also −ζ is a unit orientation of Q.
(v) If A is not injective, then [A] = 0, because the vectors Ae_j are linearly dependent (L9).
(vi) For a unit orientation ζ = ±[τ] and every m-covector β:
 - |ζ(β)| = |β(τ)| ≤ ‖β‖;
 - |(L_#ζ)(β)| = |β(Lτ_1, …, Lτ_m)| ≤ ‖L‖^m‖β‖ (L9);
 - L_#[A] = [L∘A] by definition.
(vii) normDet(L∘A) ≤ ‖L‖^m normDet(A) for every linear A : ℝ^m → ℝ^P.
 Proof: let S := B̄_1(0) ⊆ ℝ^m, so 0 < L^m(S) < ∞. By L3 and L2, normDet(L∘A)L^m(S) = H^m(L(A(S))) ≤ ‖L‖^m H^m(A(S)) = ‖L‖^m normDet(A)L^m(S).
Part B. Construction of R'.
B0 (Reductions.) Write M := R.carrier, θ := R.mult, ξ := R.orient and μ_R := R.measure.
- By aestronglyMeasurable_orient there is a strongly measurable (hence Borel) ξ̃ with ξ = ξ̃ H^m⌞M-a.e. Replacing ξ by ξ̃ does not change R.action, since the integrands agree H^m⌞M-a.e. It also keeps every IMRep field, since orients still holds a.e. So we may assume ξ is Borel.
- θ is measurable, and θ ≥ 1 on M (mult_pos).
B1 (Localization to K.)
- K is compact, hence Borel. μ_R(ℝ^P ∖ K) = ∫⁻_{M∖K} θ dH^m = 0 (withDensity_apply, Measure.restrict_restrict). Since θ ≥ 1 on M, H^m(M ∖ K) = 0.
- Put M₁ := M ∩ K. It is Borel and countably m-rectifiable (CountablyRectifiable.mono). Also I := ∫_{M₁} θ dH^m = μ_R(K) < ∞ (locallyIntegrable_mult with K compact), and H^m(M₁) ≤ I.
- Since H^m⌞M = H^m⌞M₁, R.action(η) = ∫_{M₁} θξ(η) dH^m for every m-form η.
- By A2, T_xM = Q ⟺ T_xM₁ = Q for all x and Q.
B2 (Source pieces.) Apply A6 to M₁. This gives Lipschitz F_i (with constants Λ_i), Borel B_i and constants c_i > 0.
B3 (Good source parameters.) Fix i.
- (1) By A7 (F := F_i, B := B_i, Y := M₁; here F_i(B_i) ⊆ M₁ and H^m(M₁) < ∞), T_{F_i(b)}M₁ = range DF_i(b) for L^m-a.e. b ∈ B_i.
- (2) Let Bad ⊆ M be the set of x for which there is no subspace Q with T_xM = Q and ξ(x) a unit orientation of Q. By R.orients, Bad is H^m-null (use restrict_apply' with M Borel). By A4, L^m({b ∈ B_i : F_i(b) ∈ Bad}) = 0.
- For b outside both null sets, B1 gives T_{F_i(b)}M = range DF_i(b), and L7 gives Q = range DF_i(b). Thus ξ(F_i(b)) is a unit orientation of range DF_i(b).
- Choose a Borel L^m-null set N_i containing the exceptional set (exists_measurable_superset_of_null), and replace B_i by B_i ∖ N_i. F_i(B_i ∩ N_i) is H^m-null by L2, so all conclusions of A6 persist.
Henceforth, for every i and every b ∈ B_i, ξ(F_i(b)) is a unit orientation of range DF_i(b).
B4 (Orientation on the source pieces; Simon 3.4–3.5.)
- Let G_i := L∘F_i. It is ‖L‖Λ_i-Lipschitz, and by the chain rule it is differentiable at every b ∈ B_i with DG_i(b) = L∘DF_i(b).
- For b ∈ B_i, A8(ii) (with A := DF_i(b) and ζ := ξ(F_i(b))) gives [DF_i(b)] = ε_i(b)J_{F_i}(b)ξ(F_i(b)), with ε_i(b) ∈ {1, −1} and J_{F_i}(b) > 0. Applying L_# (A8(vi)) gives J_{F_i}(b)·L_#ξ(F_i(b)) = ε_i(b)[DG_i(b)].
- ε_i(b) = 1 iff [DF_i(b)] = J_{F_i}(b)ξ(F_i(b)). Both sides are Borel functions of b (measurable_fderiv, L3, and continuity of A ↦ [A]), so ε_i is Borel.
B5 (Target pieces.)
- B_i^+ := B_i ∩ areaRegularSet(G_i) = {b ∈ B_i : DG_i(b) injective} is Borel (L3). For b ∈ B_i ∖ B_i^+, [DG_i(b)] = 0 (A8(v)).
- Apply A5 to G_i on B_i^+. This gives pairwise disjoint Borel C_{i,l} with ⋃_l C_{i,l} = B_i^+, and d_{i,l} > 0 with d_{i,l}|c − c'| ≤ |G_i(c) − G_i(c')| on C_{i,l}.
- Enumerate the pairs (i, l) by k ∈ ℕ and write F_k := F_{i(k)}, G_k := G_{i(k)}, ε_k := ε_{i(k)}, C_k := C_{i(k),l(k)} and d_k. Then:
 - A_k := F_k(C_k) are Borel (L4) and pairwise disjoint subsets of M₁, being pieces of the disjoint sets F_i(B_i) with F_i injective on B_i.
 - G_k is injective on C_k, and DG_k(c) is injective for c ∈ C_k. N_k := G_k(C_k) = L(A_k) is Borel (L4).
 - g_k : N_k → C_k, the inverse of G_k|C_k, is Borel: for Borel S ⊆ C_k, g_k^{-1}(S) = G_k(S) is Borel by L4.
 - N₀ := ⋃_k N_k is Borel, N₀ ⊆ L(M₁) ⊆ L(K), and H^m(N₀) ≤ ‖L‖^m H^m(M₁) < ∞ (L2).
 - η_k(c) := [DG_k(c)]/J_{G_k}(c) (c ∈ C_k) is a unit orientation of range DG_k(c) (A8(iii)), and it is Borel in c.
 - J_{G_k}(c) = normDet(L∘DF_k(c)) ≤ ‖L‖^m J_{F_k}(c) (A8(vii)).
B6 (Tangent spaces of the image; this fills the gap in Simon 3.7.)
- For each k, A7 (F := G_k, B := C_k, c := d_k, Y := N₀) gives an L^m-null set E_k ⊆ C_k such that T_{G_k(c)}N₀ = range DG_k(c) for c ∈ C_k ∖ E_k.
- H^m(G_k(E_k)) = 0 (L2). Let E' ⊇ ⋃_k G_k(E_k) be Borel and H^m-null.
- Let y ∈ N₀ ∖ E' and let k satisfy y ∈ N_k. Then g_k(y) ∉ E_k, so T_yN₀ = range DG_k(g_k(y)). By L7 these planes coincide for all such k; call the common plane T_y.
B7 (Reference orientation and signs; Simon 3.7–3.8.)
- For y ∈ N₀ let k(y) := min{k : y ∈ N_k}. This is Borel, since {k(y) = k} = N_k ∖ ⋃_{k'<k} N_{k'}.
- Put ξ'(y) := η_{k(y)}(g_{k(y)}(y)) on N₀ and ξ'(y) := 0 off N₀. Then ξ' is Borel, and for y ∈ N₀ ∖ E' it is a unit orientation of T_y.
- For y ∈ N₀ ∖ E' with y ∈ N_k, η_k(g_k(y)) is also a unit orientation of T_y. By A8(iv), η_k(g_k(y)) = σ_k(y)ξ'(y) with σ_k(y) ∈ {±1}. Define σ_k(y) := 1 if η_k(g_k(y)) = ξ'(y), and −1 otherwise; this is Borel on N_k.
B8 (Integer multiplicity.)
- Θ(y) := Σ_k 1_{N_k}(y)θ(F_k(g_k(y))) ∈ [0, ∞] is Borel.
- By L1 for G_k on C_k (with g := θ∘F_k∘g_k on N_k, using g_k(G_k(c)) = c), then B5, then L1 for F_k on C_k: ∫_{N_k} θ(F_k(g_k(y))) dH^m(y) = ∫_{C_k} J_{G_k}·θ∘F_k dL^m ≤ ‖L‖^m∫_{C_k} J_{F_k}·θ∘F_k dL^m = ‖L‖^m∫_{A_k} θ dH^m.
- Summing by monotone convergence, and using that the A_k are disjoint subsets of M₁: ∫Θ dH^m ≤ ‖L‖^m I < ∞. Hence Θ < ∞ H^m-a.e.
- If Θ(y) < ∞, only finitely many k have y ∈ N_k, because θ ≥ 1 on A_k ⊆ M. Then set s(y) := Σ_{k: y∈N_k} θ(F_k(g_k(y)))ε_k(g_k(y))σ_k(y) ∈ ℤ. Otherwise set s(y) := 0. s is Borel and |s| ≤ Θ.
B9 (Representation formula; Simon 3.6–3.8.) Let ω ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P) and c_ω := sup_y‖ω(y)‖ < ∞. Put φ(x) := θ(x)(L_#ξ(x))(ω(Lx)) = θ(x)ξ(x)(L^#ω(x)).
 (a) φ is Borel on M, and |φ| ≤ c_ω‖L‖^mθ H^m-a.e. on M (A8(vi) and R.orients). So φ is integrable on M₁, and R.action(L^#ω) = ∫_{M₁} φ dH^m by B1.
 (b) H^m(M₁ ∖ ⋃_i F_i(B_i)) = 0 and the F_i(B_i) are disjoint and Borel, so ∫_{M₁} φ = Σ_i∫_{F_i(B_i)} φ (integral_iUnion).
 (c) By L1 (F_i is injective on B_i) and B4, ∫_{F_i(B_i)} φ dH^m = ∫_{B_i} J_{F_i}(b)φ(F_i(b)) db = ∫_{B_i} θ(F_i(b))ε_i(b)[DG_i(b)](ω(G_i(b))) db. The integrand vanishes on B_i ∖ B_i^+ (B5). Splitting B_i^+ = ⨆_l C_{i,l} and re-indexing gives R.action(L^#ω) = Σ_k∫_{C_k} θ(F_k(c))ε_k(c)[DG_k(c)](ω(G_k(c))) dc. The double series converges absolutely: its k-th term is bounded by ∫_{A_k}|φ| dH^m (L1), and Σ_k∫_{A_k}|φ| ≤ ∫_{M₁}|φ| < ∞.
 (d) For c ∈ C_k, [DG_k(c)] = J_{G_k}(c)η_k(c). So the k-th integrand is J_{G_k}(c)ψ_k(G_k(c)), where ψ_k(y) := θ(F_k(g_k(y)))ε_k(g_k(y))η_k(g_k(y))(ω(y)) on N_k and ψ_k := 0 elsewhere. ψ_k is Borel, |ψ_k| ≤ c_ω1_{N_k}θ(F_k∘g_k) by A8(vi), and it is integrable by B8. L1 for G_k on C_k gives ∫_{C_k} J_{G_k}·ψ_k∘G_k dL^m = ∫_{N_k} ψ_k dH^m.
 (e) Since Σ_k∫|ψ_k| dH^m ≤ c_ω∫Θ dH^m < ∞, Σ_k∫ψ_k = ∫Σ_kψ_k (integral_tsum). For y ∈ N₀ ∖ E' with Θ(y) < ∞, B7 gives Σ_kψ_k(y) = Σ_{k: y∈N_k} θ(F_k(g_k(y)))ε_k(g_k(y))σ_k(y)ξ'(y)(ω(y)) = s(y)ξ'(y)(ω(y)). Off N₀ both sides vanish. Hence R.action(L^#ω) = ∫ s(y)ξ'(y)(ω(y)) dH^m(y).
B10 (The triple R'.) Put N := {y ∈ N₀ ∖ E' : Θ(y) < ∞, s(y) ≠ 0}, θ'(y) := |s(y)| and ξ''(y) := sign(s(y))ξ'(y). The fields of IMRep univ m hold:
- N is Borel, and N ⊆ N₀ ⊆ L(K) ⊆ univ.
- N is countably m-rectifiable: N ⊆ ⋃_k G_k(ℝ^m) with every G_k Lipschitz (Definition 1.1 with M₀ = ∅).
- θ' is measurable, ℕ-valued and ≥ 1 on N.
- Local integrability: ∫_{N∩C} θ' dH^m ≤ ∫Θ dH^m < ∞ for every compact C.
- ξ'' is Borel, hence H^m⌞N-a.e. strongly measurable.
- Orientation: apply A3 with A' := N ⊆ Y := N₀ (H^m(N₀) < ∞). For H^m-a.e. y ∈ N, T_yN = T_yN₀ = T_y (B6), and ξ''(y) = ±ξ'(y) is a unit orientation of T_y (B7, A8(iv)).
- Action: θ'ξ'' = sξ' on N, and s = 0 off N ∪ E' with H^m(E') = 0. So R'.action(ω) = ∫_N θ'ξ''(ω) dH^m = ∫ sξ'(ω) dH^m = R.action(L^#ω) by B9.
Thus R' := (N, θ', ξ'') is an IMRep in ℝ^P with R'.carrier ⊆ L(K) and R'.action(ω) = R.action(L^#ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P). The construction also covers the degenerate case: if every B_i^+ is empty, then N₀ = N = ∅, all sums are empty and both sides vanish. ∎
proof_key_steps: Quantitative partition (A5–A6). Mathlib's approximately linear partition with error κ_A/2 gives every piece the lower Lipschitz constant κ_A/2. So M₁ = M ∩ K is covered H^m-a.e. by disjoint bilipschitz pieces F_i(B_i).

On the source pieces ξ(F_i(b)) orients range DF_i(b), so J_{F_i}·L_#ξ(F_i(b)) = ±[DG_i(b)] with G_i = L∘F_i. This vanishes where DG_i is singular, and the regular part splits into bilipschitz pieces C_k of G_k.

(TF) for G_k gives a common tangent plane T_y of N₀ = ⋃_k G_k(C_k) for H^m-a.e. y. The signs σ_k relative to a reference orientation ξ' give the integer multiplicity s = Σ_k θ·ε_k·σ_k, which is integrable because J_{G_k} ≤ ‖L‖^m J_{F_k}.
Two area formulas turn R.action(L^#ω) into ∫ s·ξ'(ω) dH^m. Then R' = (N, |s|, sign(s)ξ'), with N = {s ≠ 0}, is an IMRep carried by L(K); its orientation property follows from locality.

subproblems.title: Linear push-forward of a compactly supported integer multiplicity current (Simon 6.2.23–2.24 and 3.9)
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (X : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) m) (R : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) m) (L : Euclid P →L[ℝ] Euclid P), 0 < m → R.Represents X → IsCompact X.support → ∃ Y : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) m, IsIntegerMultiplicity Y ∧ Y.support ⊆ L '' X.support ∧ (BoundaryVanishes X → BoundaryVanishes Y) ∧ ∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) m, Y ω = R.action (affinePullbackForm L 0 (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) m))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, 2.23–2.24 (chapter-06.txt lines 403–440: f_#T(ω) := T(ζ f^#ω) with ζ ≡ 1 near spt T ∩ spt f^#ω; ∂f_#T = f_#∂T; the integral formula 2.24(2)) and Lemma 3.9 (lines 857–860), for the linear map f = L, which is proper on the compact set spt X.
Siblings: imrep_pushforward (dimred_cs_sp_imrep_linear_pushforward), mass_support (dor_imrep_massOn_eq_measure_and_support), imrep_current (dtc_imrep_current). Notation: H^m = μHE[m], μ_R = R.measure.
1. (The carrier lives on K.) K := spt X is compact. By mass_support (U = ℝ^P), K = ℝ^P ∩ spt μ_R, so ℝ^P ∖ K ⊆ ℝ^P ∖ spt μ_R. The latter set is μ_R-null (Mathlib Measure.measure_compl_support; ℝ^P is second countable). Hence μ_R(ℝ^P ∖ K) = 0, and since θ ≥ 1 on M, also H^m(M ∖ K) = 0.
2. (Push the triple forward.) By imrep_pushforward (m ≥ 1, K compact, μ_R(Kᶜ) = 0) there is an IMRep R' = (N, θ', ξ') with N ⊆ L(K) and R'.action(ω) = R.action(L^#ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P).
3. (The current.) By imrep_current there is Y ∈ 𝒟_m(ℝ^P) with R'.Represents Y. So Y(ω) = R'.action(ω) = R.action(L^#ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P), which is the action formula. Y is integer multiplicity, with witness R'.
4. (Support.) L(K) is compact, as a continuous image of a compact set, hence closed. μ_{R'}(ℝ^P ∖ L(K)) = ∫⁻_{N∖L(K)} θ' dH^m = 0, because N ⊆ L(K). An open μ_{R'}-null set is disjoint from spt μ_{R'} (Mathlib Measure.subset_compl_support_of_isOpen). By mass_support for Y and R', spt Y = ℝ^P ∩ spt μ_{R'} ⊆ L(K) = L(spt X).
5. (Boundary.) Suppose m = k + 1 and ∂X = 0, and let φ ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^P).
 (a) ∂Y(φ) = Y(dφ) = R.action(L^#(dφ)). Also L^#(dφ) = d(L^#φ), because pull-back by an affine map commutes with d (SimonGMT exteriorDerivative_affinePullbackForm; φ is smooth).
 (b) Choose ρ > 0 with K ⊆ B(0, ρ), and a smooth bump function ζ : ℝ^P → [0, 1] with ζ = 1 on B̄(0, ρ) and tsupport ζ ⊆ B̄(0, ρ + 1) (Mathlib ContDiffBump with rIn = ρ, rOut = ρ + 1). Then ψ := ζ·L^#φ (pointwise scalar multiplication) is smooth, since L^#φ is smooth (affinePullbackForm_isSmoothForm). It has compact support in B̄(0, ρ + 1). So ψ ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^P) and dψ ∈ 𝒟^{k+1}(ℝ^P).
 (c) On the open set G := B(0, ρ) ⊇ K we have ψ = L^#φ. So for x ∈ G the two forms agree on a neighbourhood of x, their derivatives at x agree, and dψ(x) = d(L^#φ)(x), since the exterior derivative at x is computed from the derivative at x (Filter.EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq).
 (d) H^m(M ∖ K) = 0 (step 1) and K ⊆ G, so the integrands θξ(d(L^#φ)) and θξ(dψ) agree H^m⌞M-a.e. Hence R.action(d(L^#φ)) = R.action(dψ).
 (e) R represents X and dψ is a test form, so R.action(dψ) = X(dψ) = ∂X(ψ) = 0.
 By (a)–(e), ∂Y(φ) = 0 for every φ, i.e. ∂Y = 0 (BoundaryVanishes Y).
6. (Conclusion.) Steps 3–5 give the four claims:
- Y is integer multiplicity;
- spt Y ⊆ L(spt X);
- BoundaryVanishes X → BoundaryVanishes Y;
- Y(ω) = R.action(L^#ω) for every test form ω. ∎
proof_key_steps: spt X = spt μ_R (sibling mass_support), so μ_R(Kᶜ) = 0 for the compact set K = spt X.
Sibling imrep_pushforward gives an IMRep R' carried by L(K) with R'.action = R.action∘L^#. Sibling imrep_current turns it into an IM current Y with the action formula.
spt Y = spt μ_{R'} ⊆ L(K), since L(K) is closed and the open set ℝ^P ∖ L(K) is μ_{R'}-null.
∂Y(φ) = R.action(d(L^#φ)) = R.action(d(ζL^#φ)) = ∂X(ζL^#φ) = 0, for a cutoff ζ ≡ 1 near K.

subproblems.title: Projecting a compact perturbation onto V does not increase mass (Simon 7.3.1, footnote 2)
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (T X S' : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) m) (RT RX : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) m) (V : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), RT.Represents T → RX.Represents X → RT.measure ((V : Set (Euclid P))ᶜ) = 0 → IsCompact X.support → (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) m, S' ω = T ω + RX.action (affinePullbackForm V.starProjection 0 (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) m))) → ∃ R : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) m, (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) m, R.action (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) m) = T ω + X ω) ∧ ∀ O : Set (Euclid P), S'.massOn O ≤ R.measure (V.starProjection ⁻¹' O)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 of the parent proof ("S''(ω) = ∫_{M_S} θ_S⟨ω(q(x)), Λ_m q ξ_S(x)⟩ dH^m … |Λ_m q ξ_S(x)| ≤ 1 … hence |S''(ω)| ≤ μ_S(q^{−1}(W*))"). This is Simon 7.3.1, footnote 2 (chapter-07.txt lines 358–362: orthogonal projection onto the subspace does not increase area), with the push-forward formula of Simon 6.2.24(2) and 6.3.3 (chapter-06.txt lines 414–440 and 776–783). Here S' = T + q_#X, which equals q_#(T + X) because q_#T = T.
Siblings: projection_invariance (dimred_cs_sp_action_starProjection_eq), orient_projection (dimred_cs_sp_orient_projection_le), int_combination (rsdic_exists_imrep_int_combination), mass_support (dor_imrep_massOn_eq_measure_and_support).
Notation:
- H^m = μHE[m].
- For an IMRep R₀ = (M₀, θ₀, ξ₀), its vector density is v_{R₀}(x) := 1_{M₀}(x)θ₀(x)ξ₀(x) ∈ Λ_m(ℝ^P), i.e. R₀.carrier.indicator (fun y => (R₀.mult y : ℝ) • R₀.orient y).
- |β|_E = covectorEuclideanNorm β, and ‖β‖ is the operator norm of a covector β.
1. (Construction of R.) By int_combination (U = ℝ^P, R₁ = R_T, R₂ = R_X, p₁ = p₂ = 1) there is an IMRep R = (M_R, θ_R, ξ_R) with v_R = v_{R_T} + v_{R_X} H^m-a.e.
2. (Actions through vector densities.) For every IMRep R₀ and every m-form η: R₀.action(η) = ∫_{M₀} θ₀ξ₀(η) dH^m = ∫_{ℝ^P} v_{R₀}(x)(η(x)) dH^m(x). This holds because M₀ is Borel and v_{R₀}(x)(η(x)) = 1_{M₀}(x)θ₀(x)ξ₀(x)(η(x)) (Mathlib integral_indicator).
3. (Pointwise bounds.) For every IMRep R₀ and H^m-a.e. x ∈ M₀, ξ₀(x) is a unit orientation of some subspace (R₀.orients). Hence:
 (a) |ξ₀(x)(α∘q)| ≤ |α|_E for every m-covector α (orient_projection);
 (b) |ξ₀(x)(β)| ≤ ‖β‖ for every m-covector β, since ξ₀(x)(β) = ±β(τ) with τ orthonormal and |β(τ)| ≤ ‖β‖Π‖τ_i‖ = ‖β‖.
4. (Finiteness.)
 (a) For compact C, μ_{R_T}(q^{-1}(C)) < ∞. Indeed μ_{R_T}(ℝ^P ∖ V) = 0, and q^{-1}(C) ∩ V ⊆ C because qx = x for x ∈ V. So μ_{R_T}(q^{-1}(C)) = μ_{R_T}(q^{-1}(C) ∩ V) ≤ μ_{R_T}(C) < ∞ (locallyIntegrable_mult). In particular μ_{R_T}(C) < ∞.
 (b) μ_{R_X}(ℝ^P) < ∞. By mass_support, spt X = ℝ^P ∩ spt μ_{R_X}. On the second countable space ℝ^P the complement of the support of a measure is null (Mathlib Measure.measure_compl_support), so μ_{R_X}(ℝ^P ∖ spt X) = 0. And μ_{R_X}(spt X) < ∞ since spt X is compact.
5. (Additivity.) Let ω ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P), C := tsupport ω (compact), and let η be either ω or q^#ω. Let R₀ ∈ {R_T, R_X} with carrier M₀. For H^m-a.e. x:
 |v_{R₀}(x)(η(x))| ≤ c_ω·θ₀(x)1_{M₀}(x)1_D(x),
 where:
- if η = ω: D := C and c_ω := sup‖ω‖, by 3(b);
- if η = q^#ω: D := q^{-1}(C) and c_ω := sup|ω|_E, by 3(a). This is finite, as |·|_E is continuous and ω has compact support; also q^#ω(x) = ω(qx)∘q vanishes unless qx ∈ C.
The right-hand side has H^m-integral c_ω·μ_{R₀}(D) < ∞ by step 4.
